name: Inbox triage
summary: The owner, or the assistant who keeps their inbox, starts the day knowing what needs a reply today, what can wait and until when, and what belongs to someone else, with a draft or a forwarding note for each. Nothing is sent, archived, deleted or moved, and no mailbox login is needed.

sources.title: The export and paste-in form with its header check, the arrangement and order of the seven groups (several of which apply ideas credited below), the reply-by date, the private group, the question list and the acceptance tests.

sources.contribution: Ordering what needs the owner by the cost of a day's delay; pulling out the ask, amounts, who is waiting and earlier promises; asking for recent promises when only pasted mail is supplied; holding bank-detail, payment and log-in requests with no draft and checking the sender's address; leaving a thread a colleague already answered; telling a bill from a receipt; no price or date in a draft the owner has not given; reporting mail that needs no reply as one count broken down by kind, not item by item.

The drafts-only rule, routing unusual, threatening or money matters straight to the owner, undrafted, no draft where the owner has already replied, and keeping follow-ups with a status, flagging those due today or overdue even when no new message has arrived.

The split between replies due today and replies that can wait, handing a message to the colleague who should deal with it with a short forwarding note, and drafts that answer the core ask first and buy time honestly when the answer is not known.
